question.nlq: Show molecules that have many chlorine atoms, and for each such molecule report the number of single, double, and triple bonds.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term many means more than 4 chlorine atoms per molecule.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH mol_cl AS (
    SELECT molecule_id
    FROM atom
    WHERE element='cl'
    GROUP BY molecule_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 4
)
SELECT
    mc.molecule_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN b.bond_type = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS single_bonds,
    SUM(CASE WHEN b.bond_type = '=' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS double_bonds,
    SUM(CASE WHEN b.bond_type = '#' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS triple_bonds
FROM mol_cl mc
JOIN bond b ON b.molecule_id = mc.molecule_id
GROUP BY mc.molecule_id;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term many means more than 6 chlorine atoms per molecule.

    SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS chlorine_count
    FROM atom
    WHERE element = 'cl'
    GROUP BY molecule_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 6
),
bond_counts AS (
    SELECT molecule_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN bond_type = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS single_bonds,
           SUM(CASE WHEN bond_type = '=' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS double_bonds,
           SUM(CASE WHEN bond_type = '#' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS triple_bonds
    FROM bond
    GROUP BY molecule_id
)
SELECT bc.molecule_id,
       bc.single_bonds,
       bc.double_bonds,
       bc.triple_bonds
FROM chlorine_counts cc
JOIN bond_counts bc ON cc.molecule_id = bc.molecule_id;
